events.credibility_reason: Claimed positive solution of a landmark problem (it would refute Bombieri–Lang for a surface and abc-dependent results) on an unreviewed repository, with no review, comment or citation in over two and a half years; erdosproblems.com, the teorth tracker, Wikipedia (Jan 2026) and Qiu (Aug 2026) all still call the problem open without addressing it; the abstract's undefined 'method of compression' gives no sign of a technique that could get around the known arithmetic-geometry obstructions.

A blog comment carrying only a signature, pointing to a sign-in-walled Drive file; nothing posted on arXiv or in a journal; no response on the thread or anywhere else in more than two years; later status sources (erdosproblems.com with 0 proof claims, Wikipedia 2026, Qiu 2026) still call the problem open; the 1978 Chvátal attribution cannot be checked.

why: The statement asks only whether a dense planar rational-distance set exists. Results conditional on Bombieri–Lang, abc or Lang (Tao, Shaffaf, Pasten, Ascher–Braune–Turchet) reduce the question to unproven conjectures, so their scope is none. Results on curves, integer distances, finite configurations, distances to fixed points, or infinite sets lying on a circle (1945 note, Solymosi–de Zeeuw, Kreisel–Kurz, Greenfeld–Iliopoulou–Peluse, Corvaja–Turchet–Zannier, Qiu) answer changed questions, so they are variants. The only two whole-problem claims are Agama and McCallum. Both are positive constructions that nobody has read, and both meet several F10 signals together: a landmark problem, years of silence, unvetted venues, and later status sources that still call the problem open. Both are marked not_credible. The statement asks whether such a set exists, so a claimed dense set is a witness and the direction is 'confirmed' relative to the question as asked, even though it runs against the conjectured 'no'.
doubts: Agama's date cannot be placed. It was issued 9 Feb 2023, but it was only made available on the repository on 22 Mar 2024, and the record cannot say which was its first public appearance. after_snapshot is null. Neither claim's content was read: the Agama PDF could not be decoded and the McCallum file was behind a sign-in wall. The not_credible calls therefore rest on context, not on any identified error. Conditional results answered 'none' as reductions to unproven conditions.
